topics.label: Introduction and lecture learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This section serves as the lecture's opening framing by introducing the lecturer and setting out the core learning objectives.

topics.label: Foundations of cancer causation: intrinsic factors, environmental exposures, and epidemiological variation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the broad origins of cancer development by examining the interplay between intrinsic genetic mutations, environmental influences, and global epidemiological patterns.

topics.label: Mechanisms of carcinogenesis: initiation, promotion, and microenvironmental factors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the specific biological and biochemical mechanisms by which infectious agents, chemical mutagens, radiation, and inflammatory tumor promoters induce cancer.

topics.label: Methodologies for identifying carcinogens and assessing cancer risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the experimental, genomic, and epidemiological approaches used to detect carcinogenic agents and evaluate associated risks.

topics.label: Lecture summary and conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This section provides the closing framing for the lecture by reviewing the main takeaways on cancer causation and carcinogenicity assessment.
